scope: Outcome-dependent repetition counts and calibration of reliability-based Arbiter-PUF models
queries: optional stopping sample proportion bias Bernoulli

sources.title: Side Channel Modeling Attacks on 65nm Arbiter PUFs Exploiting CMOS Device Noise
sources.access: full primary PDF; relevant sections III, IV-A, IV-D
sources.overlap: Repeated response rates, noise-derived delay information, least squares; adaptive challenge selection discussed.
sources.difference: Section IV-A describes M evaluations per challenge; inspected sections do not analyze 3-or-M outcome-dependent stopping, its exact mean distortion, and count-likelihood calibration. This is a scoped comparison, not an assertion about all PUF papers.

sources.title: A Low-Dimension High-Fidelity Reliability Representation for Reliability-based Machine Learning Modeling of Physical Unclonable Functions
sources.access: primary full HTML v2, especially survey and experimental methods
sources.overlap: Reliability representations and majority-vote-enhanced PUFs; repeated response information.
sources.difference: Different problem: modeling highly reliable PUFs using LDHF. Our experiment studies variable measurement counts chosen from responses and probability calibration. We do not claim to reproduce or beat LDHF.

sources.title: PUF Side-Channel Modeling Attack Based on Confidence Weighting of Response Repeatability
sources.access: publisher abstract exposed in search; direct page blocked; full text NOT inspected
sources.overlap: Weighted least squares uses response repetition rates, probabilities and measurement counts. Generic weighting of repeated PUF observations is NOT a defensible novelty claim.
sources.difference: Abstract does not establish whether outcome-dependent stopping bias is addressed. Full-text overlap remains unresolved; must not claim exclusion.

sources.title: Properties of Estimators in Exponential Family Settings with Observation-based Stopping Rules
sources.overlap: Stopping-related estimator bias and joint likelihood theory are established general statistics.
sources.difference: General foundations, not a PUF contribution. We derive a particular 3-or-M soft-label transformation and a nonzero population-risk derivative for a probit PUF model; general optional-stopping theory is cited rather than claimed.

sources.title: On the bias of maximum likelihood estimation following a sequential test
sources.overlap: Bias after sequential sampling is known; finite-sample MLE need not be unbiased.
sources.difference: Our count-based objective has the correct stopped-path likelihood, not a guarantee of unbiased finite-sample parameter estimates.

conclusion: Original work within this project: derived stopping-law distortion and scale-score analysis, implementation, independent PUF calibration experiment. No exact counterpart located in inspected primary sections. Global novelty and priority are not proved; 2026 weighted-PUF full text remains an explicit gap.
